\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Product Bounds}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.ProductBounds
\section{Overview}
First and second coordinate Gaussian derivative kernels admit integrable quadratic majorants. Their expectations give global bounds in terms of the common variance.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{lemma}[First coordinate-score integral bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianCoordinate_first_kernel_integrable_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. If $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable with $|f|\le1$ and $i\in I$, then $z\mapsto((z_i-c_i)/v)f(z)$ is $\mu_{c,v}$-integrable and $|\int((z_i-c_i)/v)f(z)\,d\mu_{c,v}(z)|\le1+1/v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Quadratic majorant for a Hessian score]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_productHessian_mul_le}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a set, $c,z\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, $i,j\in I$, and $a\in\mathbb R$ with $|a|\le1$. Then $|(((z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v)a)|\le((z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2)/(2v^2)+1/v$, where $\delta_{ij}=1$ if $i=j$ and zero otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of the quadratic Hessian majorant]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\difficulty{1}
Let $I$ be finite, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v\ge0$, and $i,j\in I$. The function $z\mapsto((z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2)/(2v^2)+1/v$ is integrable under $\bigotimes_kN(c_k,v)$, with division by zero interpreted as zero.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integral of the quadratic Hessian majorant]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_productHessian_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_centered_sq_gaussianCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. Put $B_{ij}(z)=((z_i-c_i)^2+(z_j-c_j)^2)/(2v^2)+1/v$. For all $i,j\in I$, $\int B_{ij}\,d\mu_{c,v}=2/v$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Integrability of bounded Hessian-score products]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_productHessian_mul_le,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_bound}
\difficulty{3}
Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. For $i,j\in I$, put $H_{ij}(z)=(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is one if $i=j$ and zero otherwise. If $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ is measurable and $|f|\le1$, then $H_{ij}f$ is $\mu_{c,v}$-integrable for every $i,j\in I$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Uniform Hessian-score integral bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_integral_productHessian_mul_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_productHessian_mul_le,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_productHessian_bound,BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_productHessian_bound}
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set, $c\in\mathbb R^I$, $v>0$, and $\mu_{c,v}=\bigotimes_{i\in I}N(c_i,v)$. For $i,j\in I$, put $H_{ij}(z)=(z_i-c_i)(z_j-c_j)/v^2-\delta_{ij}/v$, where $\delta_{ij}$ is one if $i=j$ and zero otherwise. For any $f:\mathbb R^I\to\mathbb R$ with $|f|\le1$ and $i,j\in I$, $|\int H_{ij}f\,d\mu_{c,v}|\le2/v$, assigning zero to a nonintegrable integral.
\end{lemma}
